chunks: [The Admonition regarding Taqwa:] I advise you, servants of Allah, to practice Taqwa of Allah, Who clothed you with fine garments and bestowed upon you abundant sustenance;

If there was anyone who could find a ladder to permanence or a way to ward off death, it would be Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him), to whom was subjected the dominion of the jinn and humans, along with prophethood and great proximity (to Allah),

when he had consumed his due portion (of worldly provision) and completed his fixed term, the bows of destruction shot him with the arrows of death. His dwellings became vacant, his residences empty, and another people inherited them.
Indeed, in the bygone generations there is a lesson for you!
ai.seo_question: What lesson does Nahj al-Balagha draw from the life of Prophet Sulayman regarding death and worldly power?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses the archetype of Prophet Sulayman to demonstrate that even the most elevated status, combining prophethood with absolute dominion over jinn and humans, cannot exempt one from the inevitability of death. This reflection serves as a profound historical lesson (ibrah) for the believers, urging them to anchor their lives in Taqwa (God-consciousness) while worldly power remains transient. The passage underscores the Shia emphasis on using historical precedents to cultivate spiritual readiness for the ultimate return to the Creator.
